title: Conditional (and si clauses)
summary: The conditional means 'would': future stem + imperfect endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient: je jouerais, nous finirions, ils vendraient.
-re verbs drop the final e: prendre → je prendrais, attendre → il attendrait.
Irregular verbs use their future stems: je serais, j'aurais, j'irais, je ferais, je pourrais, je voudrais, je devrais, je saurais, je viendrais, je verrais.
Use it to be polite: Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît. Pourriez-vous m'aider ?
j'aimerais (I would like) and je préférerais (I would prefer) are useful for future plans: J'aimerais travailler à l'étranger.
devoir and pouvoir in the conditional mean 'should' and 'could': Tu devrais manger plus de fruits. On pourrait aller au cinéma.
Imaginary situation: si + imperfect, then the conditional: Si j'avais de l'argent, je voyagerais.
Real possibility: si + present, then the future: S'il pleut demain, nous resterons à la maison.
Never put the future or the conditional straight after si meaning 'if': Si j'avais le temps (not si j'aurais le temps).
si shortens to s' only before il and ils: s'il fait beau, but si elle vient.

cards.front: How do you form the conditional, and what does it mean?
cards.back: Future stem + the imperfect endings -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient. jouer → je jouerais, finir → nous finirions, prendre → ils prendraient. It translates 'would': je jouerais = I would play.

cards.prompt: Avec plus de temps libre, je ___ plus souvent au foot.
cards.en: With more free time, I would play football more often.
cards.why: Conditional = infinitive (the future stem) + the imperfect ending -ais: je jouerais.

cards.prompt: À ta place, je ___ le train ; c'est plus rapide.
cards.en: If I were you, I would take the train; it's quicker.
cards.why: À ta place (in your place) gives advice, so the conditional is used. -re verbs drop the e: prendr- + -ais.

cards.front: Which verbs have an irregular stem in the conditional?
cards.back: The same ones as in the future: être → je serais, avoir → j'aurais, aller → j'irais, faire → je ferais, pouvoir → je pourrais, vouloir → je voudrais, devoir → je devrais, savoir → je saurais, venir → je viendrais, voir → je verrais, falloir → il faudrait.

cards.prompt: Bonjour, je ___ deux billets pour Marseille, s'il vous plaît.
cards.en: Hello, I would like two tickets for Marseille, please.
cards.why: je voudrais (vouloir in the conditional) is the polite way to ask for something; je veux sounds rude.

cards.front: Give six useful conditional phrases for requests, advice and plans.
cards.back: Je voudrais... (I would like...), J'aimerais... (I would like...), Je préférerais... (I would prefer...), Pourriez-vous... ? (Could you...?), Tu devrais... (You should...), Ce serait génial (It would be great).

cards.prompt: Tu ___ boire plus d'eau quand tu fais du sport.
cards.en: You should drink more water when you do sport.
cards.why: devoir in the conditional means 'should': tu devrais (stem devr- + -ais).

cards.prompt: Plus tard, mon copain et moi ___ faire le tour du monde.
cards.en: Later on, my friend and I would like to travel round the world.
cards.why: mon copain et moi = nous; conditional of aimer: aimer + -ions = aimerions.

cards.instruction: Make the question more polite by using the conditional.
answers: Est-ce que vous pourriez fermer la fenêtre ?
cards.why: pouvoir has the conditional stem pourr-: vous pourriez. Pourriez-vous is the polite form of Pouvez-vous.

cards.front: Which tenses go together in a sentence with si (if)?
cards.back: Real possibility: si + present, then the future: Si tu viens, on ira au parc (If you come, we'll go to the park). Imaginary situation: si + imperfect, then the conditional: Si tu venais, on irait au parc (If you came, we would go to the park). The verb straight after si is never future or conditional.

cards.prompt: Si ma mère avait plus d'argent, elle ___ une nouvelle voiture.
cards.en: If my mother had more money, she would buy a new car.
cards.why: si + imperfect (avait) is followed by the conditional. acheter takes a grave accent in its stem: achèter- + -ait.

cards.prompt: Si nous habitions à la campagne, nous ___ un chien.
cards.en: If we lived in the countryside, we would have a dog.
cards.why: si + imperfect, then the conditional. avoir has the irregular stem aur-: nous aurions.

cards.prompt: S'il faisait beau, on ___ à la plage.
cards.en: If the weather were nice, we would go to the beach.
cards.why: si + imperfect (faisait), then the conditional. aller has the stem ir-, and on takes the il ending -ait: on irait.

cards.prompt: Si mes parents ___ riches, ils habiteraient dans une grande maison.
cards.en: If my parents were rich, they would live in a big house.
cards.why: The verb after si goes in the imperfect (ils étaient), not the conditional; the conditional (habiteraient) is in the other half of the sentence.

cards.prompt: Si ma sœur ___ à Paris, elle irait au musée tous les week-ends.
cards.en: If my sister lived in Paris, she would go to the museum every weekend.
cards.why: The main verb (irait) is conditional, so the si clause is in the imperfect: elle habitait.

cards.prompt: S'il pleut demain, nous ___ à la maison.
cards.en: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
cards.why: si + present (il pleut) for a real possibility, then the future: nous resterons.

cards.prompt: Si tu ___ faim plus tard, tu pourras manger un sandwich.
cards.en: If you are hungry later, you will be able to eat a sandwich.
cards.why: The main verb (pourras) is in the future, so the si clause is in the present: tu as faim.

cards.instruction: Make the situation imaginary: change the present to the imperfect and the future to the conditional.
cards.prompt: Si j'ai le temps, je ferai du vélo.
answers: Si j'avais le temps, je ferais du vélo.
Je ferais du vélo si j'avais le temps.
cards.en: If I had time, I would go cycling.
cards.why: Imaginary situation: si + imperfect (j'avais), then the conditional (je ferais, from the stem fer-).
